findings.description: The ok) branch derives the verdict with `jq -er '.verdict_quality.status | strings'` and compares the captured string to APPROVED. jq evaluates every top-level JSON value in the file, `-e` reports the status of the LAST output, and `$(...)` strips trailing newlines. If the captured stdout holds more than one JSON document, for example `{"verdict_quality":{"status":"APPROVED"}}` followed by any object without a string status (a progress line, telemetry, a trailing `{}`), the second document emits nothing, jq exits 0, and vq_status is exactly `APPROVED`. The phase then records completed and adds PR-VALIDATED although the envelope was ambiguous, which the new doc-comment says must fail closed as no_verdict_quality. Only the reverse ordering (APPROVED after a non-verdict object, or two statuses) fails closed. `_flatline_pr_not_green` has the mirror weakness: `jq -c '.verdict_quality'` on a multi-document file returns several lines and `--argjson vq` rejects them, so the degraded summary is dropped.
findings.failure_mode: A single stray JSON line on the Flatline orchestrator's stdout, now captured wholesale under --json, turns a non-verdict into a green PR-VALIDATED marker. The gate is only as strict as the producer's stdout hygiene, which the orchestrator does not verify.
findings.suggested_fix: Slurp and require exactly one object: `vq_status=$(jq -ers 'if length == 1 and (.[0] | type) == "object" then .[0].verdict_quality.status | strings else empty end' "$flatline_output")`, treating any other shape as no_verdict_quality. Use the same `-s` / `length == 1` discipline for the vq and degraded_models reads in _flatline_pr_not_green so multi-document files can never yield multi-line values.

findings.description: Green requires only `verdict_quality.status == "APPROVED"`. The same envelope (see the test fixture _envelope and the reads in _flatline_pr_not_green) also carries `degraded`, `degraded_models` and `blockers`, none of which are consulted on the green path. If the producer ever emits APPROVED together with a non-empty degraded_models (quorum reached after a voice was dropped) or a non-empty blockers list alongside exit 0, the phase records completed and adds PR-VALIDATED. The exit classifier only sees the exit code, so the envelope is the last line of defence and it is checked on a single field.
findings.failure_mode: A partially degraded review whose quality status still reads APPROVED is marked PR-VALIDATED, which is the one-voice-missing outcome sprint-bug-267 is meant to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: On the APPROVED path additionally require `(.degraded // false) == false and ((.degraded_models // []) | length) == 0 and ((.blockers // []) | length) == 0`; route any inconsistency to `_flatline_pr_not_green "envelope_inconsistent"`.

findings.description: `flatline_output_tmp=$(mktemp "${flatline_output}.XXXXXX")` has no failure check, unlike every other mktemp in this file (`|| return 1` or `if summary_tmp=$(mktemp ...)`). If mktemp fails (unwritable .run/, ENOSPC, EMFILE) the variable is empty, `> ""` is an ambiguous-redirect error so the Flatline orchestrator never runs, flatline_result becomes 1, and `mv -f "" ...` prints an error. The result lands in the `*` class as `exit_1`, so it fails closed only by accident and with a reason that blames Flatline rather than the harness.
findings.failure_mode: Capture-setup failures are indistinguishable from Flatline failures in the summary and logs. Any future change to how exit 1 is classified would silently remove the accidental fail-closed outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: `flatline_output_tmp=$(mktemp "${flatline_output}.XXXXXX") || { log_error "Could not create Flatline capture file"; rm -f "$flatline_stderr"; _flatline_pr_not_green "capture_setup_failed" "$flatline_output" "$degraded_summary"; return 0; }`

findings.description: After the `type == "object"` guard, `vq=$(jq -c '.verdict_quality' ...)` and `degraded_models=$(jq -c '.degraded_models // [(.verdict_quality.voices_dropped // [])[] | .voice? // empty]' ...)` run unguarded. The second expression errors when voices_dropped is a string or number (`.[]` on a non-iterable), and both yield multiple lines on multi-document input. Either case leaves an empty or multi-line value that is passed to `--argjson`, which makes the `jq -n` fail. The summary is then never written, so surface_degraded_handoff prints nothing about Flatline even though the phase is failed. The marker and phase state stay correct, but the hand-off loses the only record of status, voices and reason.
findings.failure_mode: Degraded reviews reach READY_FOR_HITL with FLATLINE-PR-DEGRADED in state but no summary or hand-off explanation, so the reviewer sees a marker with no evidence behind it.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard each read with a safe default: `vq=$(jq -c '.verdict_quality' "$f") || vq='{}'`; `degraded_models=$(jq -c '(.degraded_models | arrays) // [((.verdict_quality.voices_dropped | arrays) // [])[] | .voice? | strings]' "$f") || degraded_models='[]'`. Combine with the `-s` / `.[0]` single-document rule from SEC-001.

findings.description: The DEGRADED-convergence write composes the new summary with `--argjson previous "$previous_summary"`, redirects `jq -n` straight into summary_tmp, then `mv -f` unconditionally. If previous_summary is empty (the `jq -c` on line 714 failed after the `-e` check passed: file truncated or replaced between the two reads, I/O error) or `$iter` is ever non-numeric, `jq -n` fails and leaves an empty temp file that is moved over .run/post-pr-degraded-summary.json. Both the Bridgebuilder DEGRADED record and the Flatline summary the code was trying to preserve are lost at once. Because surface_degraded_handoff guards on `-s`, an empty file produces no hand-off warning at all. _flatline_pr_not_green already demonstrates the correct guarded pattern.
findings.failure_mode: A write error in the Bridgebuilder phase erases evidence of two degraded reviews, and READY_FOR_HITL is reached with no DEGRADED notice while state still carries FLATLINE-PR-DEGRADED.
findings.suggested_fix: Default on failure (`previous_summary=$(jq -c ...) || previous_summary='null'`), wrap the `jq -n` in the same `if jq ...; then mv -f ...; else rm -f ...; log_error ...; fi` used by _flatline_pr_not_green, and have surface_degraded_handoff warn when the summary file exists but is empty or unparseable instead of staying silent.

findings.description: phase_bridgebuilder_review now preserves any summary whose `.phase` or `.previous.phase` is flatline_pr without checking that it belongs to this run or this PR. The only places that clear the file are phase_flatline_pr and the skip branch in run_orchestration, neither of which executes when the orchestrator is started with --resume from a state after FLATLINE_PR, or when a previous PR's run died after FLATLINE_PR. A leftover .run/post-pr-degraded-summary.json from another PR is then carried under .previous and surfaced by surface_degraded_handoff as a DEGRADED Flatline review of the current PR. The direction is conservative, but the hand-off message is the control this change exists to protect, and wrong-PR attribution trains reviewers to ignore it.
findings.failure_mode: Reviewers see DEGRADED Flatline warnings for PRs whose Flatline phase was green or never ran, eroding trust in the hand-off signal that is meant to force human attention.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop a kept summary whose `.pr_number` differs from `"$STATE_SCRIPT" get pr_number`, and clear .run/post-pr-degraded-summary.json and .run/post-pr-flatline-pr.json in the state init path so a new PR never inherits them.
